heading_en: Line Head Indent and Line End Indent

cases.quote: The line head indent is the indentation of the line head by a fixed amount, starting from the line head side of the hanmen (in the case of one column) or of the column area (in the case of several columns). In contrast, the indentation of the line end position by a fixed amount, starting from the line head, is called line end indent.
cases.rationale: The rule states two indents distinct from §3.5.1's paragraph-initial one: a line head indent that narrows every line's own measure, first line included, and a line end indent that narrows the composition target from the far side. Both halves need a fixture a single-line case cannot give, because §3.5.1's own first-line indent already produces a nonzero first-line placement and a two-line paragraph is the smallest fixture that can tell the two apart on the second line. Two ideographs (亜亜, cl-19, no inter-character spacing of their own — Table 1's cl-19-against-cl-19 cell is blank, and so are its line-head row and line-end column for cl-19) on a 500-unit head indent and a 1000-unit end indent, at a 2500-unit measure, compose to exactly two one-character lines: the target is measure minus end_indent, 1500, and one 1000-unit ideograph plus the 500-unit indent already reaches that target exactly, so the second ideograph is pushed onto a line of its own rather than joining the first. Line 2's own placement is the head-indent assertion: `with_indents`' own head half narrows every line's measure and not only the first (`crate::compose::Paragraph::head_indent_for`'s own `false` branch), so the second ideograph sits at 500, not 0 — 0 is what a first-line-only indent, or a dropped `head_indent`, would report instead. The break position itself is the end-indent assertion: without `end_indent` narrowing the target, the same two ideographs at the same 500-unit head indent reach only 2500 units together, which is the plain measure, so both would fit one line and there would be no second line to carry the head-indent assertion at all — the end indent is consequently what forces the second line to exist, not merely what shortens the first.

forbidden.why: §3.5.2's own head indent narrows every line, second included; a placement of 0 on line 2 answers §3.5.1's paragraph-initial indent instead, which stops after the first line.

This is what the same input composes to when the end indent is not applied to the target: both ideographs fit one 2500-unit line. §3.5.2's own end indent narrows the target from the line end side, and a composition that reaches this shape has not narrowed it.
